newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik commander warns of more bloodshed.
newsitem.headline: Tajik commander warns of more bloodshed.

text.p: A maverick Tajik army commander warned on Tuesday the expected return of armed opposition guerrillas to Tajikistan would provoke fresh bloodshed.

Under the terms of a peace accord signed in June between the government and Islamist opposition fighters aimed at ending four years of civil war, up to 500 armed guerrillas are permitted to return to the capital Dushanbe.
"I am for the peace agreement," said Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, the commander of an elite government armoured brigade. "But the return to Tajikistan of opposition fighters will mean bloodshed."

Khudoyberdyev, who fought during the civil war against the Islamists, has often cast doubt on the peace accord. He has mutinied twice and his relations with the government of the former Soviet republic remain ambivalent.

Last month the colonel took over the southern town of Kurgan Tyube and the surrounding region's economically vital cotton plantations, placing them under the control of his own recently created "defence council".
Khudoyberdyev spoke to Reuters in the nearby town of Kalininabad, about 130 km (85 miles) south of Dushanbe, after carrying out a military exercise on Tuesday involving tanks and mortars.
"The peace agreement should be implemented with the existing (Russian) peacekeeping force," Khudoyberdyev said.
"I have tried to speak with the president (Imomali Rakhmonov) but nobody will put me through to him (by telephone)," he said.
Diplomats view the 34-year-old Khudoyberdyev as politically ambitious and a potential coup-maker whose 1,500 well-armed men give him real clout.

They and many of the 5.7 million population fear the return of opposition guerrillas could upset the fragile peace in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China. Tens of thousands lost their lives in the war and many were displaced or forced to flee the republic.
A ceasefire has held since December last year but Tajikistan is a prey to competing regional factions and armed bands.
